questions.prompt: In event-driven architecture, what is an 'event'?
options: An instruction telling a system what to do next
An announcement that something already happened, published without targeting a specific recipient
A scheduled batch job
A synchronous request that blocks until it receives a response
questions.explain: An event describes a fact that already happened, published to a channel rather than addressed to a specific recipient — the foundation of publish/subscribe thinking from Lesson 1.
questions.distractorExplain: Option A describes a command, not an event. Lesson 1's and Lesson 9's 'fact, not command' rule is exactly what separates a real event from an instruction wearing an event's clothes.

questions.prompt: What is the Pub/Sub API built on, in contrast to the CometD-based Streaming API?
options: SOAP over HTTP/1.0
gRPC over HTTP/2, with Avro-encoded payloads
GraphQL over WebSockets
FTP batch transfer
questions.explain: Pub/Sub API is built on gRPC and HTTP/2 with Avro-encoded payloads, a different technical foundation than CometD's Bayeux-based long polling.
questions.distractorExplain: Option A (SOAP) is an older, unrelated integration style covered in the Salesforce Integration Development course — it has nothing to do with either Pub/Sub API's or CometD's actual foundations.

questions.prompt: An architect is designing an Order_Confirmed__e event that an external fulfillment system will act on. The design requires the event to fire only if the surrounding Salesforce transaction actually commits. Which Publish Behavior setting should the event use?
options: Publish Immediately
Publish After Commit
High-Volume
Standard-Volume
questions.explain: Publish After Commit only fires the event once the enclosing transaction commits successfully, which is the right choice whenever a subscriber needs to trust the underlying data is durable.

questions.prompt: A CDC subscriber needs to react only when an Account record is newly created, not updated or deleted. Which changeType value should it check for in the ChangeEventHeader?
options: UPDATE
UNDELETE
CREATE
GAP_OVERFLOW
questions.explain: CREATE is the changeType value produced when a record is newly inserted; UPDATE, UNDELETE, and the GAP_* variants correspond to different operations or gap-recovery scenarios.

questions.prompt: A subscriber inserts a new Shipment_Log__c record every time it receives an Order_Shipped__e event, with no duplicate check. Given Salesforce's at-least-once delivery guarantee, what risk does this subscriber have?
options: It will never receive the event at all
A duplicate delivery of the same event will create a duplicate Shipment_Log__c record
The event will automatically be converted into a custom object
The subscriber will be unsubscribed automatically
questions.explain: An insert is not naturally idempotent, so without a processed-event tracking check, a duplicate delivery (allowed under at-least-once delivery) will create a second, unwanted log record.

questions.prompt: A company is building a standalone application, running outside any Salesforce org, that needs to subscribe to a Change Data Capture channel. Which should it use?
options: lightning/empApi
Pub/Sub API
Process Builder
Batch Apex
questions.explain: Pub/Sub API is built for external, non-Salesforce clients that need to publish or subscribe to platform events and CDC events; lightning/empApi is for code running inside Salesforce's own LWC layer.

questions.prompt: Inside an Apex test, EventBus.publish() is called between Test.startTest() and Test.stopTest(). What actually causes the subscribing trigger to run?
options: EventBus.publish() itself, immediately
Test.stopTest(), which carries out the queued publish and delivers it to subscribers
Test.getEventBus().fail()
Nothing; triggers never run inside a test context
questions.explain: EventBus.publish() only queues the event even in a test; Test.stopTest() is what actually carries out the publish and delivers it to subscribers on the test event bus.

questions.prompt: Select every true statement about Salesforce platform events.
options: Every platform event's API name ends in __e
High-volume is the default volume type for new custom event definitions since API version 45.0
Platform event records can be queried later with a SOQL SELECT, just like a custom object
A platform event automatically carries a ReplayId and an EventUuid
Platform events support lookup relationship fields just like custom objects
questions.explain: Platform events end in __e, default to high-volume since API 45.0, and automatically carry ReplayId/EventUuid. They are not queryable after delivery and don't support relationship fields like lookups.

questions.prompt: Select every field that is actually part of a CDC event's ChangeEventHeader.
options: changeType
entityName
recordIds
ReplayId
changedFields
questions.explain: changeType, entityName, recordIds, and changedFields are all part of ChangeEventHeader. ReplayId is a separate field on the overall event message, carried by every platform event, not part of the ChangeEventHeader itself.

questions.prompt: Select every true statement about choreography versus orchestration.
options: Orchestration relies on a central coordinator that explicitly calls each step in order
In choreography, each component reacts to events and may publish its own, with no central coordinator
Choreography makes it easier to see the entire process in one place than orchestration does
Event-driven designs tend toward choreography
Fan-out means a single event reaching multiple independent subscribers
questions.explain: Orchestration uses a central coordinator; choreography has none, with components reacting to and publishing events independently. Choreography actually makes it HARDER, not easier, to see the whole process in one place, since no single component holds the full sequence.

questions.prompt: Select every true statement about the Pub/Sub API.
options: It is built on gRPC and HTTP/2
It uses Avro to encode event payloads
It unifies publishing, subscribing, and schema/topic discovery into one API
A Pub/Sub API client identifies an event's unique ID via an EventUuid field
It was built by Salesforce as a successor aimed primarily at external, non-Salesforce clients
questions.explain: Pub/Sub API runs on gRPC/HTTP-2, uses Avro payloads, unifies publish/subscribe/schema discovery, and targets external clients. It does NOT have an EventUuid field — that UUID is carried in the event's own `id` field instead.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: Platform events and Change Data Capture events are retained for replay for up to ______ hours.
questions.explain: Platform events and CDC events are retained for 72 hours; a subscriber offline longer than that can no longer recover the missed events by replay.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: A platform event's API name always ends in the suffix ______.
questions.explain: Every platform event API name ends in __e, parallel to __c for custom objects/fields.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: To request that the platform retry an entire platform event trigger invocation after a transient failure, Apex code throws EventBus.______Exception.
questions.explain: Throwing EventBus.RetryableException tells the platform to retry the entire trigger invocation for the current batch of events.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: In a Pub/Sub API client (unlike a CometD client's EventUuid field), an event's unique identifier is carried in a field simply called ______.
questions.explain: Pub/Sub API clients don't have an EventUuid field; the same UUID value is carried in the event's own id field instead.

questions.prompt: Match each term to its correct definition.
right: The setting controlling whether an event fires immediately or only after the transaction commits
The metadata field carrying changeType, entityName, recordIds, and changedFields on a CDC event
A system-populated UUID uniquely identifying one specific platform event message
An event's position in its channel's stream, usable to resume a subscription after a disconnect
questions.explain: Replay ID is a stream position for resuming a subscription; EventUuid is a system-populated unique message identifier; ChangeEventHeader carries CDC's changeType/entityName/recordIds/changedFields; Publish Behavior controls immediate vs. after-commit publishing.

questions.prompt: Match each design concept to its correct definition.
right: An operation that produces the same result whether it runs once or many times
One published event reaching multiple independent subscribers, each reacting on its own
An event carrying minimal data, expecting subscribers to look up any extra detail themselves
Components reacting to events and publishing their own, with no central coordinator
questions.explain: Fan-out is one event reaching many subscribers; choreography is coordination with no central controller; an idempotent operation is safe to repeat; a thin event carries minimal data and leaves lookups to the subscriber.

questions.prompt: Match each API or tool to the use case it best fits.
right: Subscribing to platform events or CDC from inside a Lightning Web Component
An external, non-Salesforce client publishing or subscribing via gRPC and HTTP/2
Periodic, scheduled bulk processing with no single triggering event
The Bayeux-protocol-based transport that lightning/empApi subscriptions actually run over
questions.explain: empApi is the LWC-facing subscription module; Pub/Sub API serves external gRPC clients; Batch Apex handles scheduled bulk work with no single triggering fact; CometD/Streaming API is the underlying transport empApi wraps.

questions.prompt: Put these CometD client steps in the order they actually occur.
items: Client sends a handshake request to establish the session
Client subscribes to one or more channels
Client issues a long-polling connect request and waits for events
Client unsubscribes from channels it no longer needs and disconnects
questions.explain: A CometD session always follows handshake, then subscribe, then the long-polling connect/wait cycle, and finally unsubscribe/disconnect when the client is done — a handshake must succeed before anything else can happen.

questions.prompt: Put these steps of a choreographed order-fulfillment event chain in the order they occur.
items: Order_Placed__e is published when the order is created
An inventory-reservation subscriber reacts to Order_Placed__e and publishes Inventory_Reserved__e
A payment subscriber reacts to Inventory_Reserved__e and publishes Payment_Captured__e
A warehouse-notification subscriber reacts to Payment_Captured__e
questions.explain: In choreography, each component only reacts to the event before it and publishes the next one — no central coordinator holds the full sequence, which is exactly what lets a new step be added later without changing the existing components.
